title: The env-file rule does not refuse a heredoc whose prose names a sample env file while editing the env guard
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 (session_013NEJL4DPEKRiC91yHkQV7m), 15:25 CST Nov 8, possible false alarm: the env-file rule refused a builder's Bash heredoc that edited hooks/guard_env.py. The heredoc read no file; a docstring and a comment named a sample env file name (an env stem with a .py suffix) as an example. Cost: a builder on the env guard cannot write prose about the names it matches. Step env-heredoc-false-alarm (done) covered heredoc text that only writes a file, so either this form escapes it or it regressed: reproduce first. Fix shape: ignore env names inside a heredoc body written to a file under hooks/, or list the case under the decision's Known false alarms.
note: Owner item 449 a (page answer 18:39 CST Nov 8): #2315 is replaced by a new lane at round 1 that adds two narrowings: match the interpreter only as the heredoc's command word, and stop blanking after a nested backtick. #2315 goes on branch-cleanup's close list when the new PR exists.
